## Claims
- [proved] Conditional on the accepted integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation, for \(c=r-j=1\), \(p=q-i\ge2\), and \(\min(i,j)=2\), with \(d=ij\),
  \[
  Q_d\oplus Q_{d+1}\oplus Q_{d+2}
  \cong\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2,
  \]
  where
  \[
  x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad
  x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}.
  \]
  Moreover \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\) and \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\), for
  \[
  y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},\qquad y_2=s_{(i^j,2)}.
  \]
- [proved] The requested opposite-boundary truncated certificate is established: retaining \(x_2\), the complementary minor on columns \((u,z,y_2)\) has determinant \(1\), where
  \[
  u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})},\qquad z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)}.
  \]

## Strategy
Here \(a=\min(p,c)=1\) and \(b=\min(i,j)=2\). Since \(p\ge2\) and \(c=1\), the degree-\(d+2\) Schur columns are exactly
\[
(u,x_2,z,y_2);
\]
the column \(w=s_{(i^j,1,1)}\) is outside the \(q^r\)-box, while \(u\) is inside it.

The complete Pieri rows through degree \(d+2\) are
\[
h_1x_0=x_1+y_1,
\]
and
\[
h_2x_0=u+z+y_2,\qquad
h_1x_1=u+x_2+z,\qquad
h_1y_1=z+y_2.
\]
They generate the full product lattices because
\[
(A_+J)_{d+1}=A_1J_d,\qquad
(A_+J)_{d+2}=A_2J_d+A_1J_{d+1},
\]
with \(A_1=\mathbb Zh_1\), \(A_2=\mathbb Zh_2+\mathbb Zh_1^2\), and
\[
h_1^2x_0=h_1x_1+h_1y_1.
\]

With rows ordered as \((h_2x_0,h_1x_1,h_1y_1)\) and columns as
\((u,x_2,z,y_2)\), the degree-\(d+2\) matrix is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1&0&1&1\\
1&1&1&0\\
0&0&1&1
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Deleting the retained column \(x_2\) gives
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1&1\\
1&1&0\\
0&1&1
\end{pmatrix}_{(u,z,y_2)},
\qquad \det=1.
\]
Thus its row lattice is integrally complementary to \(\mathbb Zx_2\), so
\(Q_{d+2}\cong\mathbb Z\bar x_2\). The relations also give
\[
\bar z=-\bar x_2,\qquad \bar y_2=\bar x_2,\qquad \bar u=0.
\]
The degree-\(d+1\) row \(x_1+y_1\) similarly leaves
\(Q_{d+1}=\mathbb Z\bar x_1\), and \(Q_d=\mathbb Z\bar x_0\).

## Gaps
No assertion is made in degrees \(>d+2\). This certificate does not establish the all-degree quotient, ideal generation, or minimality.

## Next
A separate all-degree elimination or saturation argument is required for any global conclusion.
